questions.heading: A Model Is Variables, Constraints and an Objective, Added Lazily
questions.stem: A script creates a gurobipy model, calls addVar 50 times and addConstr 12 times, prints m.NumVars, then calls m.optimize(). What does the print show?

options.text: 50, since each addVar call adds its variable at once
options.says: gurobipy queues additions; three-projects printed 0 variables before update and 3 after.

options.text: 0, since the additions wait for the next update or optimize
options.says: Right: changes are lazy and apply at update(), optimize() or write(), as the 'before update: 0 variables' line showed.

options.text: An AttributeError, since NumVars is read only after a solve
options.says: NumVars is a model attribute readable at any time; it simply counts what has been applied, 0 here.

options.text: 62, since NumVars counts every variable and row added so far
options.says: NumVars counts variables only (NumConstrs counts rows), and only those already applied by an update.

questions.heading: Everything You Read or Write Is an Attribute
questions.stem: A nightly run sets TimeLimit to 60 seconds. Gurobi ends with Status 9 (TIME_LIMIT) and SolCount 3. What should the program do with the result?

options.text: Discard it, since a plan exists only when Status is OPTIMAL
options.says: A limit status says why the solve stopped; SolCount 3 says Gurobi kept three feasible plans.

options.text: Re-solve with DualReductions at 0, since the status is unclear
options.says: That is the step for INF_OR_UNBD (status 4); TIME_LIMIT is not ambiguous about feasibility.

options.text: Read Pi on the budget rows, since a stopped MIP returns its LP
options.says: A MIP has no Pi, stopped or not: reading it raised AttributeError in attributes.py.

options.text: Use the best plan found, and report its gap to the bound
options.says: Right: with SolCount above 0 a limit status still has a plan, to be used with its gap reported.

questions.heading: The Matrix API Takes the Model as Arrays
questions.stem: A portfolio model has 30 binaries and 20 rows, 5 of them must-do rows x_i = 1. A colleague rebuilds it with addMVar, giving those 5 projects a lower bound of 1 instead. What changes?

options.text: Nothing, since addMVar keeps every must-do as a row anyway
options.says: Bounds are not rows: the matrix model of the lesson had 9 rows against 13, the 4 must-do rows gone.

options.text: The optimum drops, since bounds are weaker than equality rows
options.says: For a binary, 1 <= x <= 1 is exactly x = 1; both GridCap models reached 22,532.

options.text: The model has 15 rows and the same optimum as before
options.says: Right: each must-do row becomes a bound, so 5 rows go and the set of allowed plans is unchanged.

options.text: The solve fails, since a binary cannot have a lower bound of 1
options.says: A binary's bounds can be tightened to [1, 1]; the matrix model solved to OPTIMAL with them.
